title: Routing & variant selection lab - catalog walkthrough
summary: AE + SE walked the Stratus ML and infra team through the model catalog UI, focused on how Redwood suggests model variants, the compatibility matrix (hardware x quantization), and the Optimize recommendations for batching/caching. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Private for PHI use cases. Action: run sample bench with Stratus dataset and share security docs/pricing.
next_steps: Diego to share bench template and sample results spreadsheet (by 2025-11-17)
Maya to send security + SOC2 summary and managed VPC checklist (by 2025-11-14)
Customer to confirm dataset access and preferred sequence lengths for bench (by 2025-11-19)
Schedule a 60-min POC scoping call with infra + security (tentative 2025-11-20)

Maya Chen: collate SOC2 excerpt + VPC onboarding checklist - 2025-11-14

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramirez - Redwood; Aisha Khan, Tom Whitaker, Priya Nair - Stratus

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll run the walkthrough with Diego, who's our infra and bench lead. quick rundowns?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: hi thanks, we've got about 45 minutes, we're really trying to understand how you pick model variants for different hardware and what the catalog recommendations mean for latency/cost. Also we need notes on private deployment.
[00:20] Diego Ramirez: great, i'll start by sharing my screen — um sorry audio only in the transcript — but, okay, first slide is the catalog view; notice how we show variants per model with little badges: fp16, int8-qat, 4bit-ptq, and a "fallback" lane.
[00:35] Tom Whitaker: can you clarify int8-qat vs ptq? we've got an internal ops constraint where retraining for qat is hard.
[00:43] Diego Ramirez: yeah, so QA T — q a t — is quantization-aware training, needs model finetune steps and infra; PTQ is post-train quant which is faster but sometimes has quality delta. Redwood flags those in the "compatibility matrix" column — we also show observed perplexity delta on your eval prompts if available.
[00:58] Priya Nair: how automated is the routing? we want to send high-priority user traffic to a higher quality variant and background jobs to cheap variants.
[01:06] Maya Chen: good question. the routing is policy driven: you can create routes by latency SLO, cost cap, or quality metric. e.g., you can set rule A: if request.userTier=="premium" -> route to fp16 dedicated pool; else route to int8 on shared. there's also automatic fallback to compatible architectures if capacity isn't available.
[01:28] Speaker 1: (mumbled) and fallback preserves prompt context?
[01:32] Diego Ramirez: yes, we try to preserve KV cache compatibility; that said when you jump between variants with different kv-layouts you may pay an orgnization cost to rewarm the cache. we show expected rewarm tokens in the console.
[01:45] Aisha Khan: we're really sensitive to latency at 99p for our triage flows. can you show a real benchmark?
[01:52] Diego Ramirez: sure, pulling the bench page — okay here's an example: we ran a 512-token generation workload across T4, A10G, and H100 with three variants (fp16, int8-qat, 4bit-ptq). numbers are median token latency and a cost per 1k tokens. Note: try-ton was mis-labeled here in the notes — it's NVIDIA Triton integration under the hood for some routes.
[02:20] Tom Whitaker: those cost deltas look big — is that per-token cost estimate including amortized GPU infra?
[02:26] Maya Chen: yes, it's Redwood's unit-economics: we combine cloud instance rent, infra overhead, and model throughput into a per-token metric. Optimize will propose batching and prefix-cache gains to lower that.
[02:36] Aisha Khan: about private deployment — we have PHI. We need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. can Redwood private support on-prem?
[02:45] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem and VPC. We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping, and we stream audit logs to your SIEM. i'll attach the SOC2 and VPC onboarding checklist after the call — quick caveat: for fully air-gapped on-prem there are additional setup steps for model transfer.
[03:05] Priya Nair: any customers doing full on-prem?
[03:08] Maya Chen: a couple in the healthcare space — we'll share references.
[03:13] Diego Ramirez: back to the catalog: the compatibility matrix maps model architecture, kernel families, and supported quant formats per hardware (e.g., A100 supports fp16/8bit-qat with kernel family X, H100 also supports 4bit dynamic kernels). We also indicate whether the runtime can do continuous batching vs synchronous single-shot.
[03:33] Tom Whitaker: about kernel families — do you pick kernels automatically or can we pin?
[03:38] Diego Ramirez: auto by default; you can pin to specific kernel versions if you want reproducibility. we make a runtime recommendation on the model page with a confidence score.
[03:46] Aisha Khan: you mentioned Optimize suggestions earlier — can you demo a sample recommendation for our use case?
[03:51] Diego Ramirez: yeah: based on a short workload sample you uploaded we simulated common seq len 256 with 2k concurrent reqs. Optimize suggested batching window 30-50ms and prefix caching for the 60% of requests that share the same prompt prefix (triage headers). That dropped per-token cost by approx 28% in the sim and increased tail latency at P99 by 12ms.
[04:17] Aisha Khan: tradeoff is acceptable if p99 stays under 220ms, which is our internal goal.
[04:21] Maya Chen: you can set SLOs and then Optimize proposes configurations that respect your SLOs while minimizing cost — it will surface explainers: which users get affected and what the quality regressions are (by prompt set).
[04:35] Tom Whitaker: is the prompt set eval automated? how do we feed our test prompts?
[04:38] Diego Ramirez: upload them as a small CSV to the bench runner or connect via our SDK. We'll run the eval across selected variants and give a diff report (ROUGE/BLEU or custom metrics you provide). the catalog UI will show small graphs of failure modes.
[04:53] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) how noisy is the bench on shared infra?
[04:56] Diego Ramirez: we run dedicated micro-batches for benches to reduce noise, and we annotate measured variance. you can also request dedicated bench runs if you want deterministic numbers.
[05:05] Priya Nair: security question — are embeddings and prompts stored? retention policy?
[05:10] Maya Chen: by default hosted API retains minimal logs for 7 days; for enterprise dedicated/private we can negotiate retention; Private gives you full control. Logs for audit can be exported to your cloud storage or SIEM.
[05:22] Aisha Khan: ok useful. can we talk about the scenario where we route to a quantized 4-bit model but need a higher-quality fallback? what's the observed quality mismatch?
[05:31] Diego Ramirez: in our evals, 4bit PTQ tends to show occasional token-level hallucinations on long-context tasks vs fp16, the catalog shows per-prompt delta. You can configure an automatic cascade: run on 4bit, if output quality score below threshold -> re-run on fp16. There is a cost and latency hit so Optimize will simulate that cascade.
[05:55] Tom Whitaker: that cascade idea sounds promising for cost controls. what's the integration surface with our existing routing layer? we have a proxy that tags requests.
[06:03] Maya Chen: you can use request metadata to drive routing rules, or call the Redwood API with route hints. we support function calling semantics too if you want structured signals.
[06:12] Speaker 1: (unclear) do you provide SDK samples for go/java/python?
[06:15] Maya Chen: yes, python/go/java/ts SDKs. we'll include snippets in the POC runbook.
[06:20] Aisha Khan: what's the timeline to run a POC? we need to show infra will hold and security signs off within three weeks ideally.
[06:27] Maya Chen: typical POC is 2-4 weeks. first week: bench and security review, second/third week pilot traffic on Dedicated or Private. we can compress some steps based on your approvals.
[06:36] Diego Ramirez: for the sample bench we need your sample prompts, expected seq lens, and desired throughput targets. We'll share the bench template now.
[06:43] Speaker 3: (murmur) do you have any recommended shortlist of models for health triage use?
[06:47] Diego Ramirez: yes — we usually recommend mid-size open models tuned for instruction, plus a compact variant for low-latency routing. On the model page we show model maturity, benchmark scores on safety evals, and a "medical-safety" tag when we've run the typical hallucination/clinical-safety prompts. we'll mark models we've run those checks on.
[07:05] Aisha Khan: can you share the medical-safety docs?
[07:08] Maya Chen: yes i'll attach the safety evals we've run and the methodology.
[07:12] Diego Ramirez: quick note: some model names get mis-transcribed by our internal tools in the logs — so double-check the slug.
[07:18] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up — recap: Diego will share bench template + runbook; Maya will send SOC2 and VPC/on-prem checklist; Stratus will provide sample prompts and retention constraints. We'll schedule a POC scoping call next week.
[07:32] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone.
[07:34] Priya Nair: thanks, good session.

[End of transcript]
